adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java — No Maven Mojo anywhere in the repo instantiates VerifyMessageProperties or calls verify(), so the collected `messages` list can never fail any real build; the "gate" only runs inside unit tests.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows changes inside `misc/theme-verifier` (adding dependencies and adding `verifySafeHtml()` logic/tests), but it does not show (or remove) any Maven Mojo/plugin wiring or any call sites of `VerifyMessageProperties.verify()`. The claim that "no Maven Mojo anywhere in the repo instantiates VerifyMessageProperties or calls verify()" is a repo-wide assertion that cannot be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:97 — sanitized.replace("<!-- -->", "")` unconditionally strips that literal substring only from the sanitizer output (not from the raw value) before the equality check, a narrow curly-brace-artifact workaround that can mask other sanitizer-introduced mismatches and weaken the exactness of the safety comparison.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly adds `sanitized = sanitized.replace("<!-- -->", "");` in `verifySafeHtml()` (after sanitizing and unescaping) and it is applied only to the sanitizer output, not the raw `value`, before `Objects.equals(sanitized, value)` is checked. This does intentionally ignore a specific sanitizer-introduced artifact (per the preceding comment), but it also means any other sanitizer-introduced `<!-- -->` differences will be suppressed and therefore not reported, reducing the strictness/precision of the comparison. That’s a real, diff-grounded review concern, though not a definitively provable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/main/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessageProperties.java:52 — verify()'s catch(IOException) cannot catch the RuntimeExceptions thrown by verifySafeHtml() (lines 70, 79), so those exceptions propagate uncaught with a less friendly, unwrapped message instead of being surfaced as a MojoExecutionException like other errors in this class

adjudication.rationale: In verify(), the try/catch only catches IOException from Files.readString(...) and verifyNoDuplicateKeys(...). The newly added verifySafeHtml() does its own file reads and, on failure, throws RuntimeException (e.g., in the two catch blocks around new FileInputStream(file) and new FileInputStream(englishFile)). Those RuntimeExceptions will bypass verify()’s catch(IOException) and propagate uncaught, so errors won’t be reported as MojoExecutionException like other failures in this class.

adjudication_records.issue_text: misc/theme-verifier/src/test/java/org/keycloak/themeverifier/VerifyMessagePropertiesTest.java:28 — No test verifies the "happy path" where translation legitimately reuses the same anchor/HTML tags as English and produces zero messages, leaving the core new sanitizer feature's success case unverified

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new HTML/anchor sanitization logic in `VerifyMessageProperties.verifySafeHtml()` and `santizeAnchors(...)`, which is intended to allow anchor tags only when they match the English source (`if (englishMatcher.find() && Objects.equals(matcher.group(), englishMatcher.group()))`). The updated tests only cover negative cases (illegal HTML in `illegalHtmlTag_en.properties`, HTML disallowed when English has none via `noHtml_de.properties`, and changed/mismatched anchors via `changedAnchor_de.properties`). There is no test asserting the success/happy path where a translation contains the same ``/`` tags as English and `verify()` returns an empty `messages` list, leaving the core new feature's intended allowed behavior unverified.
